brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc; their finances aren't public, so lean on the market ask showing modest headroom and qualify Manjushree as a second source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging, targeting ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volumes.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc range for the 28 mm induction-wad PP cap at higher volume / looser spec
priceAsk.basis: The market ask band is ₹0.55–1.20/pc with typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, and the verdict is MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec. Our current pricing sits in a band that has room to move down.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster in exchange for half the price cut — moving from 30 Days After Receipt to 15 Days After Receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹1.82 L in cash, so we need a price cut worth at least that much to make it fair for us.

brief.financialLeverage: Rachana Plastics publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit, or how tight their cash is. That means our plan leans on our own purchase data, the market ask showing headroom, and lining up a second source. Our ₹44.37 L annual spend is real money for a private packager, so they'll want to keep us — but without their numbers, we can't gauge exactly how hard to push. The smart move is to price-shop the alternates in parallel so they know we're serious about moving volume if the price doesn't come down.

evidence.point: The market ask for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec.
We spend ₹44.37 L per year with them — enough to matter to a mid-sized converter.
Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹1.82 L in cash tied up.
Paying 30 days faster would cost us ₹3.65 L in cash tied up — too rich unless the price cut is bigger.
HDPE resin import unit value is 87.61 ₹/kg, giving us a raw-material benchmark to check their price build-up.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100), specialises in pharma bottles, caps, preforms — the top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader at ₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B (73/100), strong in pails, containers, pharma — a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.role: a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Manufacturer with pan-India reach; confidence Medium — needs qualification to confirm pharma-grade capability and pricing.

risks: Rachana's finances aren't public, so we're flying blind on their stability — qualify Manjushree and Mold-Tek now so we have a fallback if Rachana stumbles or digs in.
The market ask verdict says modest headroom, not deep discounts — pushing too hard (say, below ₹0.65) may hit their floor and stall the negotiation.
We have no internal price benchmark (no bestPriceWePay) for this material, so the market ask is our only anchor — verify it with at least one alternate quote before the meeting.
Our current terms are already 30 Days After Receipt, not the worst in our book — Rachana may resist going faster unless the price cut is compelling for them.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about pricing — the market shows our caps have headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at scale, and we're spending ₹44.37 L a year with you, so let's find a number that works for both of us.
